back: 50% of purchase or short sale value for equities.
spoken: Reg T initial margin for stocks is fifty percent.

back: Settlement cycle + 2 business days: T+3 (S+2) under T+1 settlement.
spoken: Reg T payment is due two business days after settlement. Under T plus one, that's T plus three.

back: $2,000. Long purchase: deposit the lesser of cost or $2,000. Short sale: always at least $2,000.
spoken: The FINRA margin minimum is two thousand dollars. For a long buy, deposit the lesser of the cost or two thousand. For a short sale, always at least two thousand.

back: Long: 25% of LMV. Short (stock $5 or more): 30% of SMV.
spoken: Minimum maintenance is twenty-five percent long and thirty percent short.
Long account maintenance call: divide the debit by point seven five.
Short account maintenance call: divide the credit balance by one point three.

back: Equity - (50% x LMV). Credited to SMA.
spoken: Excess equity is equity minus fifty percent of market value. It goes to SMA.
Buying power is SMA times two.

back: A decline in market value. SMA falls only when used.
spoken: A falling market doesn't reduce SMA. Only using it does.

back: Equity below 50% Reg T: 50% of sale proceeds released to SMA.
spoken: In a restricted account, half of any sale proceeds goes to SMA.

back: FINRA replaced the pattern day trader rules and $25,000 minimum with risk-based intraday margin standards, effective June 4, 2026 (phase-in through Oct 20, 2027). Exam material may lag; verify.
spoken: In June twenty twenty-six, FINRA replaced the pattern day trader rule and its twenty-five thousand dollar minimum with intraday margin standards, phased in through October twenty twenty-seven. Prep materials may still test the old rule.

back: T+1 for stocks, corporate and municipal bonds (since May 28, 2024); Treasuries T+1.
spoken: Regular way settlement is T plus one for stocks, corporates and munis since May twenty twenty-four.

back: Same business day as the record date.
spoken: Under T plus one, the ex-date is the same day as the record date.

back: Buy stop: above market, protects shorts. Sell stop: below market, protects longs.
spoken: Buy stops sit above the market and protect short sellers. Sell stops sit below and protect long positions.
